historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 base year-1 revenue growth, anchored to guidance (controllable Buy yield up low double digits on an 8% Premiere+ price rise against listings flat to down low-single-digits; Commercial/New Homes and Financial Services growing high-single to low-double digits). Equity CAGR rejected as the anchor: the 60% payout and the FY26 buyback make book value a poor growth proxy for a capital-light platform.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR (7.9%) is 41% below revenue 3-yr CAGR (13.5%) and 50% below the owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR (20.8%): the gap is distributions (payout ratio 54% -> 60%, $200m buyback) not weaker economics. Flagged; equity CAGR not used.
historical_growth.notes: Group revenue and EPS series include REA India through FY25 (India revenue 129.2 in FY25, 62.2 in FY26 as discontinued); continuing-only revenue CAGRs are given separately and are the ones the projection is judged against. FY23 was a flat year (rate-rise listing downturn, continuing revenue 1,104.4 vs 1,115.6), which is why the 3-yr continuing CAGR (16.1%) overstates trend versus the 4-yr (11.6%). Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY21 242.9, FY22 380.9, FY23 338.2, FY24 439.8, FY25 506.8, FY26 596.0 (group basis, for series consistency). Owner-FCF CAGRs are within 0.3pp of reported-FCF CAGRs: SBC (~1% of revenue) is not outgrowing cash flow. FY26 EPS (4.184) is statutory including the India impairment; continuing diluted EPS was 5.101 and core continuing 5.17.

scenario_narratives.base: Yield-led growth continues at a moderating pace: the FY27 8% Premiere+ rise and add-on depth products deliver low-double-digit controllable yield growth against flat-to-down listings, Commercial/New Homes and Financial Services grow around 10%, and costs rise mid-to-high single digits, so revenue grows 9% and margins expand modestly. Listings normalise from FY28 but growth decelerates steadily to 3% as the platform matures and the ACCC keeps a lid on price escalation. Capital returns (60% payout plus periodic buybacks) continue; the model holds the count flat.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rate cuts revive Sydney and Melbourne listings from FY28, pricing power is exercised unhindered, AI-native search and valuation products create a new monetisation layer on top of depth listings, and Financial Services (Mortgage Choice, Simplicity, PropTrack) scales toward a fifth of revenue. Operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base carries the pre-SBC margin to ~71%, and Move Inc's turnaround adds unmodelled upside through the equity-accounted stake.
scenario_narratives.bear: Regulatory capture of the growth lever: after the September 2026 undertaking, the ACCC moves against REA's subscription pricing and yield growth is held to mid-single digits. A weaker property cycle (rates, tax reform debate) takes listings down for a second year, and a CoStar-backed Domain narrows the audience gap with aggressive investment, forcing REA into higher marketing and product spend. Margins compress ~5pp and the business re-rates from compounder to regulated utility-like classifieds asset.

valuation_philosophy.summary: REA is valued as what it is: a dominant, capital-light, net-cash two-sided marketplace whose value is a long stream of owner free cash flow. The base case takes management's FY27 guidance at face value and then lets growth fade to nominal GDP over ten years while margins expand only modestly; the discount rate is a plain AUD cost of equity with no ad-hoc premium, and every company-specific risk (ACCC pricing intervention, listing cyclicality, CoStar/Domain competition) is expressed in the bear flows and a 25% bear weight rather than the WACC. The India exit is treated as complete: base-year flows are continuing-operations only, and the residual India assets and the Aurum consideration sit in the bridge at fair value less costs to sell. Leases are an operating cost, associates are an asset in the bridge, and SBC is expensed once with a flat share count funded by real buybacks.
key_risks_to_valuation: ACCC intervention on subscription pricing: the single assumption the base case most depends on is continued low-double-digit yield growth; a pricing constraint moves the value toward the bear case.
Listing volumes: FY27 is guided flat to down low-single-digits with weakness in Sydney and Melbourne; a multi-year housing downturn compounds with the pricing risk.
CoStar-owned Domain investing to close the audience gap, forcing higher marketing spend and eroding the margin expansion assumed in base and bull.
Terminal value is ~55-60% of enterprise value and Gordon growth binds; each 0.5pp of terminal growth or WACC moves the base value by roughly 7-9%.

Working-capital drag from trail-commission contract assets and vendor funding is modelled at -20% of revenue growth; if Financial Services grows faster than the core, cash conversion is lower than the margin path implies.
Move Inc (20%) is carried at A$249.9m book with no observable mark; a realtor.com transaction or News Corp restructuring could reveal materially more (or less) value.
Governance: News Corp holds 62% and controls Move Inc's other 80%; related-party outcomes may not be optimised for REA minorities.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026 revenue from CONTINUING operations (REA India is a discontinued operation held for sale at 30 June 2026; FY26 AR five-year table line 11237: FY22 1,115.6 / FY23 1,104.4 / FY24 1,349.7 / FY25 1,543.6 / FY26 1,730.4)
inputs.share_count_basis: 130,859,812 fully paid ordinary shares on issue at 6 July 2026 (FY26 AR line 11305, after the $200m buyback cancelled ~1.55m shares) plus 123,269 dilutive share/performance rights (FY26 AR note 4(c), line 6110). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and REA buys shares on-market to satisfy vesting (treasury purchases $22.4m FY26), so grants do not raise the count.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: Continuing operations: group OCF 771.4 less group capex 140.7 (PPE 6.3 + intangibles 134.4) = 630.7 as in the Metrics CSV, plus 37.9 of REA India net operating and investing cash outflow (note 19(c): operating -39.9, investing +2.0) that will not recur after the Aurum sale completes in Q1 FY27.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR note 16, share-based payment expense (including discontinued operations) 16.1 (line 6493); statement of changes in equity line 5608. No cash taxes on net-share settlement are disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 in kpis); vesting is satisfied by on-market purchases recorded as treasury share purchases.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY26 interest income 18.6 (income statement line 5442; 19.0 received). Net cash is 0.6x the FCF base, below the 1x rule-of-thumb, but it is stripped anyway because the 365.6 cash pile is added to EV in the bridge; leaving both would double-count it. Cost of the choice is ~A$2/share.
inputs.buyback_note: FY26 financing activities: on-market buy-back 200.0 (completed, shares cancelled) plus 22.4 treasury share purchases for employee plans. The flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T04:14:40Z (intraday ASX print, regular session; refresh at the 06:00Z close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-denominated build. Australian 10-year government bond ~4.4% (Sept 2026) + 5.5% AUD equity risk premium x beta ~0.95 = ~9.6% cost of equity; zero bank debt (the undrawn A$200m facility is unused) so WACC = cost of equity, rounded to 9.5%. One WACC across all three scenarios: cyclicality (listing volumes), the ACCC pricing risk and CoStar/Domain competition are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. FY26 total cash outflow for leases 11.8 (note: 8.0 principal in 'Repayment of borrowings and leases' + 3.8 interest on lease liabilities, FY26 AR lines 5683/8485/8503) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (0.68% of revenue). Lease liabilities of 75.6 (8.1 current + 67.5 non-current, the entire 'Interest-bearing loans and borrowings' line; there is NO bank debt) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt: total_debt = 0, net_debt = -cash = -365.6. The Metrics CSV total_debt column carries the 75.6 lease liabilities, per the parser, so it will differ from inputs.total_debt by design. D&A for the tax base is ex right-of-use depreciation (133.0 - 7.9 = 125.1; note 10 footnote line 7203).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI deducted once, in the equity bridge at the 30 June 2026 carrying value (11.0, note 13). Continuing-operations profit attributable to NCI was 0.1 in FY26 (Planitar 38.5% and Simplicity 30% minorities are immaterial to the flows); the -32.4 NCI loss share related to the discontinued India business. Flows are modelled at 100% of continuing operations.
inputs.ebitda_basis: Reported continuing-operations EBITDA 1,090.5 includes share of losses from associates (-19.2) and impairment (-0.4). Model EBITDA excludes associates: 1,121.3 (FY26 AR core reconciliation line 977, continuing column), which is post-SBC under IFRS, so the engine's pre-SBC anchor is 1,121.3 + 16.1 = 1,137.4 = 65.7% of revenue; the engine then deducts SBC at sbc_pct_path. The associates' carrying value enters the equity bridge instead (matching-asset rule).
inputs.working_capital_note: wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE. Continuing-basis working capital consumed ~A$57-60m in each of FY25 and FY26 against revenue growth of ~A$190m (about -30% capture): Mortgage Choice trail commissions are recognised upfront as commission contract assets (650.9, +40.7 YoY) and collected over years, and CampaignAgent funds vendor marketing until settlement (receivables 403.2, +58.8 YoY). Yield-led price rises carry no such drag, so the base uses -20%, bull -15% (mix toward price/AI upsell), bear -25%.
inputs.cash_tax_note: FY26 income taxes paid 267.4 (group) against a modelled EBIT base of ~984 (27%); FY25 253.8 on ~858 (30%). Statutory 30%. Modelled at 29.5% flat: the cash-vs-book gap is timing on a growing tax base, not a structural shelter.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (Drivers route), 10-year horizon, because REA Group is an operating company (dominant two-sided property-advertising marketplace with a growing Financial Services adjacency), which the dcf-methods routing table sends to references/owner-fcf.md plus the non-US adaptations (AUD WACC, lease treatment B, NCI, matching-asset bridge, SBC-light). First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). Horizon is 10 years so margins mature before capitalisation. Base year is FY2026 CONTINUING operations after the REA India exit; all forward paths compound from that basis, so the India losses and impairment (statutory NPAT 551.6 vs core continuing NPAT 682.1) do not contaminate the projection. Cross-check: FY0 component build gives ~641 owner FCF (1,730.4 x 65.7% = 1,136.9; less SBC 16.1, lease 11.8, D&A ex-ROU 125.1 = EBIT 983.9; tax 29.5% = 290.3; NOPAT 693.6 + 125.1 - capex 140.7 - WC 37.4) against 633.9 actual continuing owner FCF, a 1% tie. Sanity multiples must be lease-consistent: ex-lease EV against EBITDA-less-lease-cash, never ex-lease EV over post-IFRS-16 EBITDA.

bear.narrative: The ACCC follows the exclusivity-clause undertaking with a constraint on subscription pricing, capping yield growth at mid-single digits from FY28; Sydney/Melbourne listings fall a further year on rate rises and the negative-gearing/CGT debate; a CoStar-funded Domain forces higher marketing and product spend, compressing the pre-SBC margin to 61.5% by year 4. Revenue growth settles at 2.5-3% nominal; terminal cap lowered to 15x for a structurally slower, regulated business (Gordon 14.6x at 9.5%/2.5% binds just under it).

base.narrative: FY27 +9% on guidance (low-double-digit yield growth net of flat-to-down listings and geographic mix, plus ~10% in Commercial/New Homes and Financial Services), decelerating to 3% nominal by year 10 as pricing power is exercised but tempered by ACCC scrutiny. EBITDA margin (pre-SBC, ex-associates) expands 0.7pp in FY27 on mid-to-high single-digit cost growth per guidance, then ~0.5pp a year to 68.5% by year 6 and holds. Capex drifts from 8.1% toward 7.5% as the platform rebuild and AI product investment normalise; D&A held at the ex-ROU 7.2%. Gordon binds (15.8x terminal FCF at 9.5%/3.0%, under the 20x cap).

bull.narrative: Listings recover from FY28 on RBA easing, low-double-digit yield growth holds without ACCC intervention, AI products (conversational search, agentic assistant, PropTrack AVM) add a new monetisation layer, and Financial Services compounds at mid-teens. Operating leverage takes the pre-SBC margin to 71% (REA ran ~70% on the pre-Mortgage-Choice mix). Terminal growth 3.5% nominal; Gordon 17.3x binds under the 20x cap.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the growth thesis rests on a single regulator's tolerance of price-led growth: the ACCC has already extracted one undertaking (September 2026) and FY27 guidance leans on an 8% price rise against falling listings in REA's two most valuable markets. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once: a listing recovery, no further regulatory action, and AI product monetisation beyond depth listings. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
